title: Chicken Cacciatore
subtitle: Italian hunter's chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, and olives
excerpt: Chicken pieces braised slowly in a sauce of tomatoes, red peppers, black olives, capers, and white wine. A rustic Italian dish that improves with time and is better the day after making.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pollo alla Cacciatora (hunter's chicken) is a rustic Italian braise found across central and northern Italy. The name means 'in the style of the hunter', referring to a simple country preparation using ingredients to hand. There are many regional variants: the Roman version uses white wine, tomatoes, peppers, and capers; the Florentine version adds rosemary and sometimes anchovy. The common thread is chicken braised in an acidic sauce until completely tender. Using bone-in, skin-on pieces is important: the bones add flavour to the braise and the skin protects the meat from drying out.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to hold all the chicken pieces in a single layer.

content.text: Brown the chicken skin-side down first and do not move it until it releases easily: a properly browned skin will not stick. The braise should be at a gentle simmer with the lid slightly ajar: a full boil toughens the meat. Taste the sauce before adding the olives and capers: both are salty, and the sauce may not need more seasoning.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken. Brown skin-side down for 5 to 6 minutes until golden. Flip and brown for 3 minutes more. Remove from the pan.

In the same pan over medium heat, cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the red pepper and garlic. Cook for 5 minutes more. Pour in the wine and bubble for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, rosemary, and thyme.

Nestle the chicken pieces back into the sauce. The liquid should come about halfway up the chicken. Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook on the lowest heat for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Add the olives and capers. Cook for 5 minutes more. Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove the herb sprigs. Serve with polenta, mashed potato, or crusty bread.
